Makes it practical to add more LogTrace() statements in the future and lets operators toggle trace logging without restarting.

result.summary: This PR replaces the `-loglevel` startup option with a new `-trace` option that mirrors `-debug` syntax (e.g. `-trace=net` enables both debug and trace logging for the net category), and extends the `logging` RPC with a `trace` parameter and a new three-array (excluded/debug/trace) output format, preserving the old format behind `-deprecatedrpc=logging`. It also includes internal logging API cleanup (dropping string-based Enable/Trace/DisableCategory helpers in favor of `SetCategoryLogLevel`) and a locking change around `ShrinkDebugFile`. Two related PRs (internal API refactor, STDLOCK annotations) were split out during review at ryanofsky's suggestion.
result.problem: Trace-level logging previously required combining `-debug=cat` with the undocumented `-loglevel=cat:trace` syntax, and could not be toggled without a node restart via RPC; this makes tracing effectively unused (only one `LogTrace` call exists in the codebase today) and hampers future low-level debugging.

open_concerns: ryanofsky's approach NACK: three interacting options (-debug/-trace/-debugexclude) are confusing and some configurations (default trace with per-category debug override) are impossible under this design; he proposes a single `-loglevel`-style option in #35387 instead.
maflcko asked about status/milestone given the unresolved dispute; milestone was removed from 32.x as a result.
resolved_concerns: stickies-v's earlier concern about renaming 'include' to 'debug' in the RPC was addressed with an aliasing scheme preserving backward compatibility.

result.card: This PR replaces the -loglevel startup option with a -trace option matching -debug syntax, and extends the logging RPC to expose trace-level control with a new three-array output format, preserving old behavior behind -deprecatedrpc=logging. The stated problem is that trace logging is currently unusable in practice (only one LogTrace call exists in the codebase) because turning it on requires an obscure combination of -debug and -loglevel. Two reviewers (stickies-v, sedited) have approved the current code after extensive review, but ryanofsky has posted an approach NACK arguing the three interacting options (-debug/-trace/-debugexclude) are confusing and that a simpler single-option design (his alternative PR #35387) should be used instead; the author disagrees but the dispute is unresolved, and maflcko pulled the PR from the 32.x milestone as a result. The code itself is clean (no rebase needed, CI passing) but the unresolved approach dispute could still reshape the PR's design before it lands.
